questions.question: What two circumstances left the people of Laish without anyone to rescue them?
choices: They lived far from Sidon and had no ties with anyone else.
Their allies were fighting elsewhere and their own warriors had been sent away.
Sidon refused their appeal for help and neighboring towns feared the Danites.
Their messengers were captured and the roads into the valley were blocked.
questions.target: The two circumstances that prevented Laish from receiving rescue: distance from Sidon and lack of ties with others.
questions.reason: The stem explicitly requests two independently gradable circumstances: geographical remoteness and lack of outside relationships. All four options supply paired explanations for the absence of rescue, so the choices are on target.
questions.published_chinese_question: 哪两种情况使来士人得不到援救？

questions.question: What did the old prophet instruct his sons to do, and what did he do next?
choices: He instructed his sons to saddle the donkey, and then he went and found the body lying in the road.
He instructed his sons to saddle the donkey, and then he went and found the lion eating the body.
He instructed his sons to bring the body home, and then he went and prepared a place for its burial.
He instructed his sons to drive the lion away, and then he went and led the donkey back home.
questions.target: The instruction the old prophet gave his sons and the action he took next.
questions.reason: The stem asks two independently gradable questions: what he instructed and what he did next. A and B both describe saddling the donkey and then going and finding the body; they differ in whether the lion was eating it, an observation rather than a different next action.
